# Lockers and traction control

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Connect air line to port 2 and route power wires from a switch to the ARB M205 Air Locker solenoid coil. [t457]

[Partial] Transfer the old ring gear onto an ARB RD180 Front Locker after removing the entire front differential assembly. [t881]

[Partial] Install a drop-in Lunchbox Locker with new spider gears and dampening for 33-inch tires. [t882]

Allow automatic lockers to engage with forward or reverse torque for 100% power delivery. [t882]

[Partial] Remove the drop-in locker to revert the carrier back to an open or limited slip state. [t882]

Install a front locker to provide maximum traction when 4WD is engaged. [t882]

Fit a drop-in lunchbox locker into the front differential housing. [t882]

[Partial] Install an M205 locker into the R180 front differential. [t882]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Connect the air compressor line to port 2 on the solenoid.
2. [Partial] Route power and ground wires from a switch to the solenoid coil.

_Procedure reported by [t457]._

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t881] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Remove the entire front differential assembly from the vehicle.
2. [Partial] Transfer the old ring gear onto the new locker unit.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t882] [Partial]</summary>

1. Install a drop-in locker mechanism into the stock differential carrier.
2. [Partial] Replace the spider gear set and sometimes the side gears with new components.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t882] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Allow the automatic locker to engage when forward or reverse torque is applied.
2. Let both wheels receive 100% power during engagement for solid axle connection.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t882] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Remove the drop-in locker to revert the carrier back to an open or limited slip state.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t882] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Install an M205 locker into the R180 front differential.

</details>

## Parts

- Air Solenoid Valve [t457]
- ARB M205 Air Locker (RD224) [t457]
- ARB RD180 Front Locker: Available in 3.54 and lower gearing; low-speed version, RD180 available for 3.69 gears. [t881]
- Front Locker: ARB or similar automatic locking differential [t882]
- Lunchbox Locker: Drop-in style replacing spider gear set; For use in weaker aluminum housings [t882]
- M205 Locker: Features larger gears than standard setup [t882]

## Specifications

- **Tire size support limit**: 33 inches [t882] ([Unverified] single report)

## Tips & gotchas

- Port 1 on the solenoid is for input from the compressor. [t457]
- Polarity of the electrical current likely does not matter as the electromagnet self-adjusts when reversed. [t457]
- [Partial] Use the locker primarily when crawling to relieve sudden stress on spider gears. [t881]
- Note that locking both front wheels together may help prevent one wheel from spinning while the other gains traction. [t881]
- [Partial] Use dampening mechanisms if available to reduce backlash. [t882]
- [Partial] Expect smoother operation than full carrier lockers due to reuse of stock parts. [t882]
- [Partial] Drive style must adjust to handle the 'spool' effect where inside wheel spins slower. [t882]
- [Partial] Expect un-predictable handling characteristics, especially in shorter wheelbase vehicles. [t882]
- Ideal for vehicles mildly modified with slightly oversized tires. [t882]
- Consider a first 'economy' option before committing to full carrier lockers. [t882]
- [Partial] Best used on the front end where hubs can be locked and unlocked. [t882]
- [Partial] Run the locker unlocked all the time to improve strength and prevent grenading. [t882]
- Larger gears reduce the chance of shearing and sending chunks through the aluminum case. [t882]
